notes.title: How the cuisine filters were policed
notes.body: Every food card names a specific dish — a cuisine label alone doesn’t qualify. Discovery started from what is unique to Chicago: deep-dish and tavern-style thin crust, Italian beef, the Chicago-style hot dog and the Maxwell Street Polish, the Puerto Rican jibarito, mild-sauce chicken and rib tips, the Rainbow Cone and Garrett popcorn — then the immigrant corridors: Pilsen and Little Village (Mexican), Chinatown, Devon Avenue (Indian & Pakistani), Argyle (Vietnamese), Ukrainian Village and the Polish Northwest Side, Swedish Andersonville. A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it happens to serve.

notes.title: Web-searched, merit-measured and fact-checked
notes.body: Every place is traceable to at least two credible sources — or one institutional authority (Michelin, James Beard, the National Park Service, UNESCO) — recorded in data/sources.json: the Chicago Tribune, Sun-Times, Chicago Magazine, Eater Chicago, The Infatuation, Block Club Chicago, WTTW, Time Out, Choose Chicago, Atlas Obscura and vetted creators (direct page fetches are blocked in the build environment, so sources were confirmed via search). Yelp and TripAdvisor never count. Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked.

days.label: Suggested by the guide from sourced picks — check hours before you go. Distances are straight-line, not walking routes.

skipped.SW: only 3 open, verified places within 3 km of each other

mix.note: Pop culture = sights in the city’s pop-culture collections; a place counts in one segment only.

sources.note: Citations, not places: a place named by three sources counts three times. "Added by the guide" marks general-knowledge additions and is never relabelled as sourced.

perArea.note: Every place counted once, in its own area.

spread.note: Computed from 365 of 367 places: open, with a verified pin. Straight-line, not walking routes. Areas with fewer than 2 such pins are not drawn.

closed.note: Closed places stay in every view, flagged, and never carry a tier. "unchecked" = no status check on record yet.

canon.title: Chicago classics
canon.note: Bars count canon places whose own write-up names the dish; a place naming two dishes counts in both bars. Canon places that name no dish are not counted.

tiers.note: 2 closed places carry no tier and are counted in the closures chart instead.

places.w: One of the world's great art museums — 300,000 works including Seurat's La Grande Jatte, Hopper's Nighthawks and Wood's American Gothic.

places.ad: 1400 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
places.w: The 1893-born natural history museum on the Museum Campus — home of SUE the T. rex and Máximo the titanosaur.
The 103rd-floor observation deck of the former Sears Tower, with The Ledge glass boxes 1,353 ft over Wacker Drive.

places.ad: Millennium Park, 201 E Randolph St, Chicago, IL 60602
places.w: Anish Kapoor's mirror-polished 'Bean' in Millennium Park — the requisite Chicago selfie, beside Gehry's Pritzker Pavilion and the Lurie Garden. Free.
places.k: public art sculpture icon park free

places.w: The 1916 pier stretching into Lake Michigan, with the 200-ft Centennial Wheel, the Chicago Children's Museum and boat departures.
Grant Park's 1927 Versailles-inspired fountain, one of the largest in the world, with summer light-and-water shows. Free.

places.ad: 1300 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
places.w: The first planetarium in the Western Hemisphere (1930), at the tip of Northerly Island's peninsula with a classic skyline view.
The 1869 limestone water tower that survived the Great Chicago Fire, now a free city art gallery on the Mag Mile.

places.ad: 5700 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60637
places.w: The largest science centre in the Western Hemisphere, in the 1893 World's Fair Palace of Fine Arts — U-505 submarine, coal mine, Pioneer Zephyr.
The Cubs' ivy-walled ballpark (1914), the second-oldest in the majors, with its hand-turned scoreboard and Wrigleyville rooftops.

places.ad: 300 N Central Park Ave, Chicago, IL 60624
places.w: Jens Jensen's 1908 'landscape art under glass' — one of the largest conservatories in the US, with free admission.
One of the country's oldest zoos (1868) and still free, with the Farm-in-the-Zoo and Nature Boardwalk.
Frank Lloyd Wright's 1910 Prairie School masterpiece in Hyde Park, inscribed by UNESCO in The 20th-Century Architecture of Frank Lloyd Wright. Tours by the FLW Trust.
places.k: frank lloyd wright prairie school house

places.w: The 1897 former public library, now the nation's first free municipal cultural center — under the world's largest Tiffany glass dome (38 ft, ~30,000 pieces).
Burnham & Root's 1888 LaSalle Street landmark, whose skylit light court was remodelled by Frank Lloyd Wright in 1905 — the spiral oriel staircase is the money shot.
places.k: architecture building frank lloyd wright landmark

places.w: The 1921 French Baroque movie palace under the six-storey C-H-I-C-A-G-O marquee on State Street.

Hood & Howells' 1925 Gothic tower from the 'most beautiful building in the world' competition, its base studded with ~150 fragments of famous buildings (Westminster Abbey, the Great Wall, the Parthenon).
The tapering, X-braced former John Hancock Center (1969), with the 94th-floor 360 Chicago observation deck and TILT.
Bertrand Goldberg's 1963 'corncob' towers on the river — at opening the tallest residential and tallest concrete buildings in the world.
Frank Gehry's ribbon-steel bandshell in Millennium Park — free summer concerts (Grant Park Music Festival) and movies on the lawn.
Frank Lloyd Wright's 1908 poured-concrete temple in Oak Park — part of UNESCO's 20th-Century Architecture of Frank Lloyd Wright inscription.

places.n: Frank Lloyd Wright Home and Studio
places.w: Where Wright lived and worked 1889–1909 and developed the Prairie style; a National Historic Landmark, toured by the Frank Lloyd Wright Trust.
places.k: frank lloyd wright prairie school house

places.ad: 11141 S Cottage Grove Ave, Chicago, IL 60628
places.w: George Pullman's 1880s company town — the clock-tower factory, Hotel Florence and rowhouses; site of the 1894 strike and the Pullman porters' story. NPS unit since 2015.
The lace-domed 1953 Baháʼí temple on the Wilmette lakefront — the oldest surviving Baháʼí House of Worship in the world, with formal gardens.
Pilsen's free museum of Mexican art — one of the largest Latinx cultural institutions in the US (10,000+ works); its Día de Muertos show is a city ritual.
Founded 1961 in Washington Park — the oldest independent African American museum in the country.
One of the largest contemporary art museums in the world, in Streeterville off the Mag Mile; Tuesday summer jazz on the terrace.
The city's history museum at the south end of Lincoln Park — Lincoln's deathbed, the Great Fire, and an exhibit on the Chicago hot dog.
Chicago's oldest and largest continuously running blues club (1968) — two stages, alternating sets until 4 a.m.
The South Loop blues club owned by Buddy Guy himself — live blues every night and his own January residency.
One of the city's best-known jazz rooms, two blocks off the Mag Mile, with nightly sets and jam sessions.
Uptown's 1907 former Capone-era speakeasy, one of the oldest continuously operating jazz clubs in the country; home of the Uptown Poetry Slam.
places.k: jazz club speakeasy cocktail bar music

places.w: Old Town's improv theatre (1959) that launched Belushi, Murray, Fey, Colbert and Carell.

places.ad: Washington Park community area, Chicago (per Wikipedia)
places.w: Olmsted & Vaux's 372-acre South Side park, home of Lorado Taft's 'Fountain of Time' and the DuSable museum.

places.ad: Evanston lakefront, IL (per NPS NHL record)
places.w: Château-style 1894 lakefront mansion of Nobel laureate and US Vice President Charles G. Dawes — a National Historic Landmark run by the Evanston History Center.

places.ad: Lower West Side (Pilsen), around 18th St, Chicago (per Wikipedia / City of Chicago landmark district)
places.w: National Register district of 1870s–1910s Bohemian worker cottages, storefronts and churches — now the heart of Mexican Pilsen and its murals along 16th and 18th Streets.

places.ad: 300 N Central Park Ave, Chicago, IL
places.w: The 1928 Spanish Baroque 'Gold Dome' fieldhouse, a gold-leafed Chicago Landmark towering over Garfield Park — under a $9M restoration.

places.ad: 11211 S St Lawrence Ave, Chicago, IL
places.w: Pullman's 1882 serpentine-greenstone church, designed by Solon S. Beman as part of the model town.
The ensemble theatre founded in 1974 by Gary Sinise, Terry Kinney and Jeff Perry — Tony-winning home of Malkovich, Metcalf and 'August: Osage County'.

places.n: Old Town School of Folk Music
places.w: Folk-music school and concert hall (founded 1957) in a restored 1929 library building on Lincoln Square's main street.

places.ad: 2045 N Lincoln Park West (in Lincoln Park), Chicago, IL
places.w: The last tomb left from the old City Cemetery under Lincoln Park — Ira Couch's 1858 mausoleum, too heavy to move.

places.ad: Forest Ave, Oak Park, IL (per Wikipedia)
places.w: Frank Lloyd Wright's 1902 Prairie-style house on Forest Avenue — low roman-brick walls and a raised main floor, a National Historic Landmark.
places.k: frank lloyd wright prairie school house

places.n: Roberts Temple Church of God in Christ
places.w: Bronzeville church where Mamie Till-Mobley held her son Emmett Till's open-casket funeral in 1955 — part of the Emmett Till and Mamie Till-Mobley National Monument (2023).

places.ad: 2700 S Halsted St area (former Stearns Quarry), Bridgeport, Chicago (per Wikipedia)
places.w: A 1830s limestone quarry turned 27-acre park — a fishing pond in the pit, terraced wetlands and the city's best skyline hill.

places.ad: New City / Back of the Yards, Chicago (per Wikipedia)
places.w: Olmsted Brothers & Burnham 'neighbourhood park' (1905) ringed by a lagoon, with a Burnham-designed fieldhouse — a landmark of the South Parks reform movement.

places.ad: Back of the Yards, Chicago (per Wikipedia)
places.w: One of the first 1905 South Parks small parks, built to give stockyards families a fieldhouse, baths and playgrounds.

places.ad: South Fork of the South Branch, Chicago River (headwaters, per Wikipedia)
places.w: The stockyards' notorious waste channel — Upton Sinclair's 'Bubbly Creek' still burps methane from century-old sediment, now ringed by new trails.
Historic African American cemetery — resting place of Emmett Till, Dinah Washington and Willie Dixon.

places.ad: 1600–1800 blocks of W 104th Pl (Griffin Place), Beverly, Chicago
places.w: A street of Prairie School houses (1909–14), seven by Walter Burley Griffin — later the designer of Canberra — a Chicago Landmark district.

places.ad: Ukrainian Village, Chicago, IL 60622 (street number pending re-verify)
places.w: 1915 Neo-Byzantine cathedral modelled on Kyiv's St. Sophia — its thirteen copper domes crown Ukrainian Village; interior mosaics are among Chicago's finest.

places.ad: Logan Blvd, Kedzie Blvd & Palmer Sq around Logan Square, Chicago, IL 60647
places.w: The Northwest Side's grandest stretch of Chicago's boulevard system — graystone 'boulevard of the millionaires' mansions around Logan and Palmer squares (NRHP + Chicago Landmark district).

places.n: National Museum of Puerto Rican Arts and Culture
places.ad: Humboldt Park (1895 park stables), Chicago, IL 60622
places.w: The only US national museum devoted to Puerto Rican art, in Humboldt Park's 1895 stables — the park's oldest building.

places.ad: Milwaukee / North / Damen six-way intersection, Wicker Park, Chicago
places.w: The triangular 1929 Art Deco Northwest Tower — first skyscraper of its size outside downtown — at the six-way Milwaukee/North/Damen crossing, now a hotel with skyline rooftop bars.
Mother church of Chicago Polonia (1867–81, Patrick Keely) — by 1897 the largest parish in the US; a 'Polish Cathedral' landmark in Noble Square.

places.ad: Pierce Ave & Hoyne Ave around Wicker Park, Chicago, IL 60622
places.w: Victorian mansions of 'Beer Baron Row' (Hoyne) and Pierce Ave lining the 1870 park — one of the city's best post-Fire residential streetscapes (Chicago Landmark district).

places.ad: Alta Vista Terrace, Lakeview (Wrigleyville), Chicago, IL 60613
places.w: 'Street of Forty Doors' — a single block of London-style rowhouses (1900–04) mirrored end to end; Chicago's first designated historic district (1971), steps from Wrigley Field.

places.ad: W Argyle St, Uptown, Chicago, IL 60640
places.w: Where Charlie Chaplin made 'His New Job' and Gloria Swanson started out — the 1907 silent-film studio's terracotta-trimmed home, a Chicago Landmark (now St. Augustine College).
Brewer Francis Dewes's 1896 Lincoln Park mansion — exuberant German Baroque, with caryatids holding up the balcony; a Chicago Landmark beside his brother's matching house.
Freethinkers' cemetery founded 1877 by Czech immigrants — Bohemian-art monuments, Mayor Anton Cermak's grave and the Eastland-disaster victims; CAC-toured.
Olmsted & Vaux's 1869 curving-street suburb along the Des Plaines River — one of America's first planned communities, a National Historic Landmark (expanded 2023).
Wright's own 'most successful of my houses' (1906–09) — a long, low U-shaped Prairie complex set into Olmsted's Riverside; National Historic Landmark (private, exterior view).

places.n: Ward W. Willits House (Frank Lloyd Wright)
places.w: Widely considered Wright's first mature Prairie-style house (1901–02), on Highland Park's Sheridan Road — a National Historic Landmark (private, exterior view).

places.ad: 1200 S Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
places.w: 1930 Beaux-Arts aquarium on Museum Campus — 32,000 animals, beluga whales and Pacific white-sided dolphins in the lake-view Abbott Oceanarium.

places.ad: N Michigan Ave between Randolph St and Monroe St, Chicago, IL 60602
places.w: The 24.5-acre front lawn of Chicago (2004) — Cloud Gate, Crown Fountain, Gehry's Pritzker Pavilion and the hidden Lurie Garden, with free summer concerts.

places.ad: E Erie St, River North, Chicago (Nickerson Mansion)
places.w: The 1883 Nickerson 'Marble Palace' — marble floors, grand staircases and Gilded Age decorative arts, a block off Michigan Avenue.

places.ad: S Wentworth Ave, Chinatown, Chicago, IL 60616
places.w: The 1928 On Leong Merchants Association building — pagoda towers, green tile roofs and terracotta, Chinatown's signature landmark (Chicago Landmark 1993).

places.ad: S Wabash Ave, Bronzeville (Near South Side), Chicago
places.w: Home of Chicago's oldest Black congregation (1844), an Underground Railroad station; its 1892 sanctuary still stands at Bronzeville's northern edge (Chicago Landmark).
Birthplace of gospel music — Thomas A. Dorsey's 1931 choir here launched Mahalia Jackson and a new American sound (Chicago Landmark 2011).

places.n: Site of the Great Chicago Fire (Pillar of Fire)
places.w: Where the 1871 fire began in the O'Leary barn — now, fittingly, the CFD's Quinn Fire Academy, with Egon Weiner's bronze 'Pillar of Fire' and a plaque marking the spot (Chicago Landmark).

places.ad: Lakefront from North Ave to Ardmore Ave, Chicago (Chicago Park District)
places.w: Chicago's largest park (1868) — seven miles of lakefront with the free zoo, conservatory, North Pond, Caldwell Lily Pool, beaches and the Lakefront Trail.

places.ad: N Clark St around Foster & Balmoral Aves, Andersonville, Chicago
places.w: The old Swedish village on Clark Street — indie shops, Swedish bakeries and the flag-painted water tower; Time Out once voted it the coolest neighbourhood in the US (NRHP district).

places.ad: N Sheridan Rd at the north end of Lake Shore Drive, Edgewater, Chicago
places.w: The pink 1928 tower at the end of Lake Shore Drive — the surviving sister of the vanished Edgewater Beach Hotel resort (NRHP).

places.ad: 900–1100 blocks of W Bryn Mawr Ave (Sheridan Rd to Broadway), Edgewater, Chicago
places.w: Three blocks of 1897–1928 apartment hotels and terracotta façades once home to Chicago's elite — Bryn Mawr & Belle Shore hotels; made a Chicago Landmark district in Sept 2026.
An 1886 limestone 'Irish castle' on the Beverly ridge, built by developer Robert Givins for his bride — home of Beverly Unitarian Church since 1941.
181-acre East Side lakefront park with a sandy beach, a 1924 Classical Revival fieldhouse (Chicago Landmark) and a model-train exhibit; views to the Indiana steel shore.
Chicago's oldest public building (1856) and a Great Fire survivor — Celtic-revival windows and Book of Kells-inspired stencils in the West Loop.

places.ad: S Dearborn St at W Adams St, the Loop, Chicago
places.w: Holabird & Roche's 1895 Chicago School landmark — Tiffany mosaics of Père Marquette's voyage and Edward Kemeys bronzes in the lobby.

places.ad: N Michigan Ave, the Loop, Chicago (Pendry Chicago hotel)
places.w: The Burnham brothers' 1929 black-granite and gold-leaf Art Deco tower — said to be modelled on a champagne bottle — now the Pendry hotel with a rooftop bar.
Chicago's oldest house (1836), the Greek Revival home of Henry & Caroline Clarke, now a city-run museum in the Prairie Avenue district.
The city's architecture HQ on the river — supersized skyscraper models, the lit-up downtown model, and the departure dock for its famous 90-minute First Lady river cruise.

places.ad: S Michigan Ave, Prairie Avenue district, Chicago
places.w: Gothic Revival church re-done inside in Arts & Crafts style by Howard Van Doren Shaw after a 1900 fire — 21 stained-glass windows, nine by Tiffany (NHL).

places.ad: W Washington St, the Loop, Chicago
places.w: The 1924 First United Methodist 'Chicago Temple' — the world's tallest church building, with a tiny Sky Chapel in its spire 400 ft above the Loop.

places.ad: Irving Park — blocks around Avers & Hamlin Aves north of Addison St, Chicago
places.w: Seven boulevard blocks of 126 Prairie & Craftsman bungalows (1907–25) with double lots and deep setbacks — a hidden NRHP + Chicago Landmark district.
Rapp & Rapp's 1930 Gateway movie palace, restored as the Polish-American Copernicus cultural centre — concerts and dance most nights; next door to the Taste of Polonia festival.
America's leading museum of outsider and self-taught art — home of the recreated Henry Darger Room; reopened in 2025 after a major expansion.
Chicago Landmark district of worker cottages and two-flats around the onion-domed churches — the heart of the city's Ukrainian community (CAC walking tour).

places.n: Frank Lloyd Wright Historic District (Oak Park)
places.w: The world's largest concentration of Wright buildings — two dozen Prairie houses within walking distance of his Home & Studio; FLW Trust guided walks April–November.
places.k: frank lloyd wright architecture historic district

places.w: Northwestern's free art museum on the lakefill campus — prints, photography, film and ambitious exhibitions.
1929 glasshouse with 20,000 plants in Mediterranean, tropical and desert rooms — a free hidden gem south of downtown Oak Park.

places.ad: W Jackson Blvd between Laflin St and Ashland Ave, Near West Side, Chicago
places.w: A block of 1880s Victorian rowhouses and mansions that survived the West Side's decline — a Chicago Landmark district and NRHP listing.
1929 town hall at the heart of Austin — now a Chicago Park District cultural centre and fieldhouse with a historic auditorium.

places.ad: W Argyle St between Broadway and Sheridan Rd, Uptown, Chicago
places.w: Chicago's 'Little Saigon' — a few blocks of pho houses, bakeries and Asian markets around the Argyle 'L' stop (NRHP historic district; Asia on Argyle night market).

places.ad: Division St / Milwaukee Ave / Ashland Ave, Wicker Park–Noble Square, Chicago
places.w: The plaza at the heart of old 'Polish Downtown', where nearly every major Polish-American organisation once had its headquarters — summer 'Tuesdays at the Triangle' events.
385 acres on nine islands in the Cook County Forest Preserves at Glencoe — 24 gardens, prairies and greenhouses; the winter Orchid Show.
The 216-acre Chicago Zoological Park in Brookfield — polar bears, the Seven Seas dolphins, Tropic World.
The 2.7-mile elevated rail-trail through Logan Square, Humboldt Park, Wicker Park and Bucktown. Free.

places.ad: 6401 S Stony Island Ave (Wooded Island, Jackson Park), Chicago, IL 60637
places.w: The Japanese garden on Jackson Park's Wooded Island, rooted in Japan's 1893 World's Fair pavilion; 160 cherry trees in spring. Free.
Victorian garden cemetery (1860) of Chicago's builders — Burnham, Sullivan, Mies, Marshall Field, Roger Ebert — with Lorado Taft's 'Eternal Silence'.
The Bears' colonnaded 1924 lakefront stadium (with its 2003 'spaceship' bowl), also home of the Chicago Fire.

places.n: Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures Museum
places.w: The University of Chicago's free museum of the ancient Near East (ex-Oriental Institute) — the 40-ton Khorsabad lamassu, Egypt, Persia, Mesopotamia.
The University of Chicago's soaring Gothic chapel, with a 72-bell carillon among the largest instruments ever built.

places.ad: 5491 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60615
places.w: Alfred Caldwell's limestone-stepped peninsula with a castle-like field house — a downtown-skyline view, swimming off the rocks and fire pits. Free.

places.ad: 7059 S South Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60649
places.w: The 1906 South Shore Country Club, now a Park District cultural center with a beach, nature sanctuary and golf — the Obamas held their wedding reception here.
H. H. Richardson's 1887 Romanesque fortress-house on Prairie Avenue, a museum of the Gilded Age.

places.ad: 50 E Ida B. Wells Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
places.w: Adler & Sullivan's 1889 Auditorium Building — a National Historic Landmark with a gold-leafed arched hall and famous acoustics.
Burnham & Root's 1891 load-bearing brick skyscraper — 'the first modern building' — with Holabird & Roche's steel-frame 1893 addition.
The 1925 Beaux-Arts station whose Great Hall rises under a 219-ft barrel-vaulted skylight — the Untouchables staircase.
The 1890s Victorian glasshouse in Lincoln Park — palms, ferns and orchids, free and open year-round.
15 miles of Lake Michigan beaches and towering dunes an hour from the Loop by the South Shore Line — Mount Baldy, the West Beach dune trails.
Sandstone canyons and seasonal waterfalls on the Illinois River, 90 minutes south-west of Chicago — Illinois's most-visited state park.
The two surviving buildings of Jane Addams's 1889 settlement house on the UIC campus — the birthplace of American social work. Free (suggested donation).
North America's oldest outdoor music festival — the Chicago Symphony's summer home; picnic on the lawn.
1,700 acres of trees in Lisle with 16 miles of trails and a children's garden; Illumination in winter.

places.ad: 700 N Art Museum Dr, Milwaukee, WI 53202
places.w: Calatrava's lakefront Quadracci Pavilion whose Burke Brise Soleil 'wings' open and close daily — 90 minutes north of Chicago.
The only Harley-Davidson Museum in the world — 450+ motorcycles on a 20-acre Menomonee Valley campus.
Louis Sullivan's only intact house of worship (1903), a Russian-village church in Ukrainian Village, part-funded by Tsar Nicholas II.

places.ad: 3100 W Logan Blvd (Logan Square), Chicago, IL 60647
places.w: The eagle-topped column at the heart of Logan Square (1918), by Henry Bacon of the Lincoln Memorial — the hub of the boulevard system.
One of the oldest and largest ethnic museums in the US (1935), in the old Polish Downtown.
Rapp & Rapp's 1925 'acre of seats in a magic city' — the largest movie palace ever built in Chicago, shuttered since 1981 and awaiting restoration (exterior only).
The 1926 Spanish-palace dance hall with a twinkling-star ceiling, now a rock venue.
The 1929 Southport movie palace with a starry-sky ceiling and a live organist between shows — Chicago's leading independent cinema.
The 1914 Lincoln Avenue movie house outside which John Dillinger was shot by the FBI in 1934; now Victory Gardens' stage.

places.ad: Washington Park, 5900 S Cottage Grove Ave, Chicago, IL 60637
places.w: Lorado Taft's 1922 concrete procession of 100 figures passing before Father Time, at the west end of the Midway. Free.

places.ad: 6760 S Stony Island Ave, Chicago, IL 60649
places.w: Theaster Gates's restored 1923 bank — the Johnson Publishing library, Frankie Knuckles' records, galleries and free events.
places.k: gallery arts library house music free

places.w: Mies van der Rohe's 1956 glass-and-steel architecture school at IIT — widely held to be his finest work; a National Historic Landmark.

places.ad: 3500 S Dr Martin Luther King Jr Dr, Chicago, IL 60653
places.w: Bronzeville's 1928 memorial to the Black 8th Illinois regiment (370th Infantry) of WWI, won by a Chicago Defender campaign.
The 1879 Burnham & Root limestone gate — all that remains of the 475-acre Union Stock Yards that made Chicago 'hog butcher for the world'. A National Historic Landmark; free.
Where Martin Luther King Jr. marched for open housing in 1966 (and was struck by a rock); the Living Memorial's three pillars at Marquette Rd & Kedzie tell the Fair Housing story. Free.
The only museum in North America devoted to Lithuanian history and culture — in the city with the most Lithuanians outside Lithuania.

places.ad: Millennium Park, 201 E Randolph St, Chicago, IL 60602
places.w: Jaume Plensa's twin 50-ft glass-block towers in Millennium Park, projecting faces of Chicagoans who spout water into the splash pool. Free.
places.k: fountain public art park free family

places.ad: Daley Plaza, 50 W Washington St, Chicago, IL 60602
places.w: Picasso's untitled 50-ft Cor-ten steel sculpture (1967) in Daley Plaza — baboon, woman or dog, he never said. Free.

places.ad: Federal Plaza, 50 W Adams St, Chicago, IL 60603
places.w: Alexander Calder's 53-ft red stabile (1974) set against Mies van der Rohe's black Federal Center. Free.

places.ad: Chase Tower Plaza, 10 S Dearborn St, Chicago, IL 60603
places.w: Marc Chagall's 70-ft mosaic box (1974) of six Chicago scenes in 250 colours. Free.
20 acres east of Millennium Park — the climbing walls, the winter skating ribbon, mini golf and a giant playground. Free.

places.ad: Chicago River (main branch), Lake St to Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60601
places.w: The 1.25-mile path along the river's main branch — wine bars, kayak rentals and the city's best architecture at water level. Free.
Independent research library (1887) facing Washington Square — free exhibitions from 1.6 million books and 600,000 maps.
The world's largest public library building at opening (1991), with owl-topped acroterions and a 9th-floor winter garden. Free.
Chinatown's riverside park on an old rail yard — pagoda pavilion, kayak launch and the water-taxi stop. Free.
Small Chinatown museum on the Chinese journey to the Midwest, in the old Quong Yick warehouse.
Pilsen's 1892 hall modelled on the Prague opera house, now one of the city's favourite music venues (with Dusek's downstairs).
The Sunday open-air flea market descended from the 1880s Maxwell Street bazaar — tools, tires, produce and some of the city's best street tacos.
The Chicago Academy of Sciences' museum in Lincoln Park, built around the 2,700-sq-ft Judy Istock Butterfly Haven.

places.ad: Montrose Harbor (W Montrose Ave & Lake Shore Dr), Chicago, IL 60640
places.w: 15 lakefront acres where 300+ migratory species stop at 'the Magic Hedge'. Free.
Col. Robert McCormick's 500-acre Wheaton estate — gardens, his mansion, and the First Division tank museum.

places.n: Illinois Holocaust Museum and Education Center
places.w: Stanley Tigerman's Skokie museum founded by survivors, with its pioneering interactive survivor-hologram theatre.

places.ad: 339 N Oak Park Ave, Oak Park, IL 60302
places.w: The Queen Anne house where Hemingway was born in 1899, restored as a museum.
Evanston's 1873 lighthouse on the lake bluff, a National Historic Landmark; summer weekend tours.

places.ad: Forest Home Cemetery, 863 S Des Plaines Ave, Forest Park, IL 60130
places.w: The 1893 monument over the graves of the executed Haymarket anarchists — a pilgrimage site for May Day; surrounded by 'Radical Row'. National Historic Landmark.

places.ad: 373 W Geneva St, Williams Bay, WI 53191
places.w: The 1897 'birthplace of modern astrophysics' on Geneva Lake — home of the world's largest refracting telescope; tours.
Frank Lloyd Wright's 1939 'dendriform'-columned Great Workroom and Research Tower in Racine — free tours by reservation.

places.ad: 1600 N Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60614
places.w: Chicago's busiest beach, by Lincoln Park — the ocean-liner beach house, volleyball, paddleboards and the classic skyline-across-the-sand view. Free.

places.ad: 1000 N Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60611
places.w: The Gold Coast beach at the top of the Mag Mile, tucked under the skyline. Free.

places.ad: 1200 S Linn White Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
places.w: Small crescent beach on Northerly Island behind the Adler, with panoramic lake views. Free.

places.ad: 1521 S Linn White Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
places.w: The man-made peninsula (the old Meigs Field) re-wilded with prairie paths, fishing spots and skyline views. Free.
Jens Jensen's 207-acre park — the Prairie School boathouse and swan boats on the lagoon, and the 1895 stables now housing the National Museum of Puerto Rican Arts & Culture. Free.
Ukrainian Village museum of folk art, pysanky (Easter eggs) and immigrant history.
The domed 1892 French-Romanesque church of the city's old French parish, in Little Italy/University Village.
The presidential museum, library branch and tower in Jackson Park, opened Juneteenth (June 19) 2026 — timed tickets sold out months ahead.
The 1924 white-terracotta twin towers with a Giralda-style clock tower — the first skyscraper on the new Michigan Avenue, floodlit at night.
Holabird & Root's 1930 Art Deco tower closing the LaSalle Street canyon, crowned by John Storrs's faceless aluminium Ceres.
The Archdiocese's 1875 Gothic Revival cathedral by Patrick Keely, with the cardinals' galeros hanging from the ceiling.
Frank Lloyd Wright's 1915 cubic Prairie house in Rogers Park — tours via the FLW Trust, and you can even stay overnight.
places.k: frank lloyd wright prairie school house

places.w: Andersonville's 1976 museum of Swedish immigrant history and art, with a children's immigration museum upstairs.
Rapp & Rapp's 1917 Balaban & Katz movie palace in the Uptown theatre district, now a rock venue.
The 1912 Victoria vaudeville house in Lakeview, now a concert hall that has hosted Bowie, Pearl Jam and Coldplay.

places.ad: Longwood Dr & W 103rd St (Beverly), Chicago, IL 60643
places.w: One of the largest urban districts on the National Register — 3,000+ homes on the glacial ridge of Beverly and Morgan Park by Wright, Maher, Griffin, Burnham and Shaw; walk Longwood Drive past the Givins 'Irish castle'. Free.
places.k: historic district architecture house frank lloyd wright prairie school free

places.w: Third Ward food hall of ~20 vendors — brats, squeaky cheese curds, seafood, Thai — named one of America's best public markets by Frommer's.
Riverside craft brewery (1987) that helped revive Milwaukee brewing — its comic tour and Friday fish fry are city rituals.
Captain Frederick Pabst's 1892 Flemish Renaissance Revival mansion, restored and open for tours.
Lakeshore science-and-technology museum with the Reiman Aquarium and a tall ship.
The 1860 Gothic Revival church that survived the Great Fire (the O'Learys were parishioners) — the second-oldest Catholic church in Chicago.
Garfield Park's 1902 Renaissance Revival basilica with a gold-leafed barrel vault — one of three papal basilicas in Chicago (WTTW's 'Most Beautiful Places').
Jens Jensen's own favourite work (1915–20) in Austin — a prairie river, council rings and stone waterfalls interpreting the Illinois landscape. Free.
The 71-acre 1901 park named for the assassinated president — lagoon, trails and an outdoor ice rink. Free.
Home of the Bulls and Blackhawks; the 'Spirit' Michael Jordan statue stands in the atrium by Gate 4.
The White Sox's 1991 ballpark across 35th Street from old Comiskey, with the exploding scoreboard and fireworks after every Sox homer.

places.ad: Kirk Rd & Pine St, Batavia, IL 60510
places.w: The national particle-physics lab on the prairie — a bison herd since 1967, Wilson Hall and mathematical sculptures; grounds free with photo ID.

places.ad: 3624 S Dr Martin Luther King Jr Dr, Chicago, IL 60653
places.w: The 1889 Romanesque house where Ida B. Wells lived 1919–30 — a National Historic Landmark (private; view from the street).
Avondale's 1917 Polish 'cathedral' — a papal basilica since 2003 and the heart of Chicago's Polish Village.
Bucktown's block-long Polish Renaissance church (1920) modelled on St. Peter's, its dome ringed by angels.

places.ad: Mt. Baldy Beach, US-12, Michigan City, IN 46360
places.w: The 120-ft living dune at the east end of Indiana Dunes National Park — the largest moving dune on Indiana's shore (summit by ranger-led hike).

places.ad: 1 Heisman Harbor Rd (Washington Park), Michigan City, IN 46360
places.w: The 1858 Michigan City lighthouse, now a museum in Washington Park by the beach and harbour.
Starved Rock's quieter neighbour — canyon dells and waterfalls about two hours from Chicago.

places.n: Wolf Lake (William W. Powers State Recreation Area)
places.w: The 800-acre lake straddling the Illinois–Indiana line in Hegewisch — otters, beavers, swans and fishing amid the old steel landscape. Free.

places.ad: 222 W Merchandise Mart Plaza, Chicago, IL 60654
places.w: The 1930 Art Deco 'Mart' on the river — once the largest building in the world, with Jules Guérin murals inside and Art on the Mart projections on its facade at night.
Louis Sullivan's 1899–1904 Carson Pirie Scott store at State & Madison — the cast-iron prairie-foliage entrance rotunda is the masterpiece.
Atwood's 1895 terracotta-and-glass tower — a prototype of the glass skyscraper and the Chicago window (now a hotel).
Jeanne Gang's 2009 tower whose rippling white balconies look like water cascading down its sides.
Chicago's oldest continually operating hotel — the gilded lobby ceiling and Tiffany fittings; birthplace of the brownie.
The domed 1926 Beaux-Arts memorial in Lincoln Park — marble rotunda, Eugene Savage murals and heroic friezes; one of WTTW's 'Most Beautiful Places'. Free.
Caldwell's 1938 Prairie-style 'hidden garden' in Lincoln Park — stratified stone, a prairie river and a waterfall; a National Historic Landmark, open April–October. Free.
places.k: garden park prairie school landmark free

places.ad: 217 S Home Ave, Oak Park, IL 60302
places.w: George W. Maher's 1897 John Farson House — an early Prairie-style mansion and National Historic Landmark, open for tours.
Living-history village of 30 historic buildings and costumed interpreters telling a 19th-century Illinois town's story.
Ukrainian Village's storefront indie-rock club — cheap shows, free Mondays, a bar cat and the midwinter Music Frozen Dancing fest.
A century-old frame house tucked into an industrial corridor (once bootleggers' turf) — beloved for concerts, variety shows and comedy.
Wrigleyville's 1927 theatre turned rock club (since 1982) — midsize touring acts upstairs, Smart Bar downstairs.
Adler & Sullivan's 1890 synagogue turned the church where Thomas Dorsey's choir gave birth to gospel music; burned in 2006, its stone walls still stand (a gospel museum is planned).
Anthony Overton's 1929–31 Art Deco terracotta newspaper building in Bronzeville, now the Chicago Bee branch library.
The University of Chicago's always-free art museum in Edward Larrabee Barnes's limestone buildings.
Frank Lloyd Wright's 1897 Isidore Heller house in Hyde Park, a step toward the Prairie style (private; view from the street).
places.k: frank lloyd wright prairie school house

places.w: Chicago's oldest and largest not-for-profit theatre (1925), in the Loop theatre district.

places.ad: 800 E Grand Ave (Navy Pier), Chicago, IL 60611
places.w: The Tony-winning Shakespeare company at the end of Navy Pier.

places.ad: 20 N Upper Wacker Dr, Chicago, IL 60606
places.w: Samuel Insull's 1929 Art Deco 'throne' on the river, its gilded hall home to the Lyric Opera since 1954.
Orchestra Hall (1904) on Michigan Avenue, home of the world-famous Chicago Symphony Orchestra.
The German parish's Romanesque church rebuilt inside its fire-scarred walls after 1871 — Bavarian Baroque interior and Munich glass.
Chicago's largest cemetery (350 acres), entered through William Boyington's castle-like gate — Victorian monuments and mausoleums.

The Taylor Street original (1938) where the family claims the Italian beef was invented; the beef for every Al's is still roasted here. #1 on the Infatuation's Italian-beef ranking and a fixture of every Chicago beef list.

places.ad: 7500 W North Ave, Elmwood Park, IL 60707
places.w: Elmwood Park walk-up open since 1961 — Steve Dolinsky's (ABC7 Hungry Hound) #1 Italian beef in the suburbs, with an 'ambrosial' jus, and the lemon ice that closes every order.
Lincoln Park's pan-pizza bar whose pies are ringed with blackened, caramelized cheese — the deep dish many Chicagoans name first (Infatuation) and #8 on Time Out's citywide pizza ranking.
The family that helped invent deep dish (Lou worked at Uno before opening his own in 1971); Infatuation calls it the best version of the classic Chicago pie — sauce on top, flaky buttery crust.
Edgewater carryout doing a focaccia-like sourdough deep dish; on both the Infatuation deep-dish ranking and Time Out's top pizza list.
Ashburn's tavern-pizza shrine since the 1940s — #1 on Time Out's citywide pizza ranking ('the king of tavern-style') and the spot with the most 'best' nods in Chowhound's tavern-pizza research.
Logan Square brewpub-bakery; on Time Out's top-pizza ranking and the only brewpub on Chowhound's tavern-pizza list.
The 1948 carhop drive-in under the two giant hot-dog mascots on the roof — on both the Infatuation and Time Out best-hot-dog lists.

places.ad: 2720 N River Rd, River Grove, IL 60171
places.w: River Grove stand (1946; here since 1950) — no seats, no ketchup; the gold standard of the Depression dog on both the Infatuation and Time Out hot-dog lists.
West Ridge stand famous since 1967 for its sign — a giant hot dog on a fork — and a char dog both the Infatuation and Time Out rank among the city's best.
Cheap, late Depression-dog stand on Armitage — on both the Infatuation and Time Out hot-dog lists.

places.ad: 1017 W Irving Park Rd, Chicago, IL 60613
places.w: Classic Wrigleyville hot-dog stand serving the North Side since 1975 — reviewed by the Infatuation and on Time Out's best-hot-dogs list.
Founded 1954 by the Lemons brothers and still family-run; South Side aquarium-smoker rib tips. 2025 James Beard America's Classics award. James Beard America's Classics Award, 2025.
Uptown Hong Kong barbecue house near Argyle, family-run since 1987; 2018 James Beard America's Classics award.
German restaurant and bar in the Loop since 1898 — its bar held Chicago's first post-Prohibition liquor license. A James Beard America's Classics honoree.
Smokehouse shack by the 95th Street bridge on the Calumet River since 1948, wood-smoking fish on site. A James Beard America's Classics honoree.
Old Town rib tavern open since 1932 (a Sinatra hangout), neon beer signs intact — on the Infatuation's old-school list and Chicago Magazine's Iconic Eats for its baby backs.
Ice-cream parlor and candy shop at Armitage & Western since 1921 — the Infatuation's old-school list and Chicago Magazine's Iconic Eats (hot fudge sundae).
River North steakhouse in its wood-frame building since 1941 — as old-school as Chicago gets (Infatuation), rib eye on Chicago Magazine's Iconic Eats.
South Loop cafeteria deli since 1942, lunchroom of generations of politicians — reviewed by the Infatuation ('still great after 80 years') and on Chicago Magazine's Iconic Eats for its corned beef.

Family-run Archer Heights birrieria devoted to Jalisco-style roasted goat. Michelin Bib Gourmand; birria on Chicago Magazine's Iconic Eats. (TEMPORARILY CLOSED as of Oct 2026 per Michelin/Apple listings — check before going.)

places.ad: 430 N Michigan Ave (lower level), Chicago, IL 60611
places.w: Lower Michigan Avenue newspapermen's tavern since 1934 — 'cheezborger, cheezborger, no Pepsi, Coke' of SNL fame and the Cubs' goat curse.
Deep-dish institution since 1966 near the Mag Mile, its cornmeal-crust pies served in graffiti-covered booths diners are invited to sign.
The River North beef stand (since 1979) that inspired The Bear's Original Beef of Chicagoland — dipped beef with hot giardiniera.
Beverly's pink stand serving its five-flavour sliced cone since 1926 — a South Side institution (Choose Chicago) and one of Chicago Magazine's 50 Iconic Eats.
Stephanie Izard's Randolph Street flagship (2010) that made the West Loop a dining district — the pig-face plate is one of Chicago Magazine's 50 Iconic Eats.
Paul Kahan's cedar-lined Mediterranean wine bar (2003) — its chorizo-stuffed, bacon-wrapped dates are one of Chicago Magazine's 50 Iconic Eats.
Greektown's taverna since 1971 — flaming saganaki ('Opa!') is one of Chicago Magazine's 50 Iconic Eats.
Skokie deli opened in the 1960s as a hub for Holocaust survivors — one of Chicagoland's oldest Jewish delis; bagel and lox on Chicago Magazine's 50 Iconic Eats.
Lincoln Park's late-night char-dog stand (to 4am weekends), as famous for the staff's good-natured verbal abuse as for its dogs.
Humboldt Park bakery run by the same family since 1911 — custom cakes, strudel, coffee cake and paczki.
The traders' bar in the Board of Trade lobby, notorious for a 'jack and coke' that's a giant cup of whiskey with the can on the side.
The taproom attached to Goose Island's production brewery (brewing here since 1995) — test batches and Bourbon County Stout rarities.
West Loop tasting-menu restaurant tied to a family farm — Chicago's only three-Michelin-star restaurant in the 2025 guide.
Grant Achatz's Lincoln Park landmark of modernist cooking, 20 years old — two Michelin stars in 2025 (down from three).
Curtis Duffy's Fulton Market tasting room — two Michelin stars; its GM Amy Cordell won Michelin's 2025 service award.
Ukrainian Village Filipino bakery-by-day, tasting-menu-by-night — raised to two Michelin stars in 2025.
Lee Wolen's Lincoln Park flagship by the Steppenwolf — one Michelin star.
Jenner Tomaska and Katrina Bravo's Lincoln Park 'atelier' restaurant — one Michelin star.
Zach Engel's modern Middle Eastern restaurant in Lincoln Park — one Michelin star.
Rick Bayless's fine-dining room behind Frontera Grill in River North — one Michelin star.
South Loop brewery whose dining room above the brewhouse holds one Michelin star.
Wicker Park's punk tasting counter — no servers, loud rap, wild cooking; one Michelin star.
Sujan Sarkar's River North modern-Indian tasting room — one Michelin star.
Chicago's newest one-star in the 2025 Michelin guide, which also gave it a Green Star for sustainable practice.
Uptown restaurant cooking the food of the Zapotec Sierra Norte of Oaxaca — Michelin Bib Gourmand.
Pasta shop and restaurant — Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2024 and 2025.
Zubair Mohajir and Rishi Kumar's colorful Indian-Mexican Bucktown restaurant — new Michelin Bib Gourmand 2025.
Reopened CDMX-style taqueria from Marcos Ascencio and Oliver Poilevey — Michelin Bib Gourmand 2025.
Noah Sandoval's hidden West Loop tasting room behind a freight elevator — two Michelin stars (2025).
Intimate Lincoln Square tasting-menu room — one Michelin star.
Phillip Foss's freewheeling Douglas Park tasting menu where diners wander into the open kitchen — in the Michelin Guide.
Rick Bayless's 1987 River North original that put regional Mexican cooking on America's map — in the Michelin Guide.
The 1923 diner at the start of Route 66 — free Milk Duds and donut holes while you wait for double-yolk eggs; in the Michelin Guide.
Grant Achatz's Fulton Market restaurant that reinvents its whole menu and theme every few months — in the Michelin Guide.
David and Anna Posey's Danish-inflected West Loop restaurant with an open-air fireplace courtyard — in the Michelin Guide.
Julia Momosé's Japanese cocktail bar and dining room in the West Loop — in the Michelin Guide.
Joe Frillman's farm-driven Logan Square pasta restaurant (own 30-acre farm) — Michelin Bib Gourmand and Green Star.
Bucktown's family-run Costa Rican restaurant — casados, gallo pinto, oatmeal shakes; 'extremely affordable and incredibly good' (Infatuation).
Andrew Zimmerman's West Loop dining room in a 19th-century print shop — one Michelin star (2025).
An Arts & Crafts warming shelter on a Lincoln Park pond turned seasonal-Midwest tasting room with a skyline view — in the Michelin Guide.
Norman Fenton's Uptown Latin American tasting menu and 'taco omakase' — Michelin-starred (Time Out's 2024 star list) and in the 2025 guide.
West Loop omakase counter — a Michelin-recognised Japanese tasting menu.
River North live-fire Middle Eastern restaurant — Michelin Bib Gourmand.
All-plant kitchen named a Michelin Bib Gourmand (Chicago 2024).
Stephanie Izard's Peruvian rooftop in the West Loop — Michelin Bib Gourmand (Chicago 2024).
Bridgeport gastropub — a Michelin Bib Gourmand in both the 2024 and 2025 Chicago lists.
Low-key Pilsen restaurant for Northern Thai fare — Michelin Bib Gourmand.
Logan Square's tiny, always-full New American — Michelin Bib Gourmand (Chicago 2024).
Logan Square salumeria/café — Michelin Bib Gourmand (Chicago 2024).
Logan Square's pioneering farm-to-table café (since 1999) — Michelin Bib Gourmand and on Eater Chicago's 38 essential restaurants.
Diana Dávila's Logan Square antojería — Michelin Bib Gourmand and one of Eater Chicago's 38 essential restaurants.
Wicker Park/Noble Square Asian-American small-plates spot — Michelin Bib Gourmand (Chicago 2024).
Hyde Park Neapolitan pizzeria on 55th St — Michelin Bib Gourmand (Chicago 2024).
River West Korean-American restaurant (401 N Milwaukee) on Michelin's 2024 Chicago Bib Gourmand list.
Pilsen pub famous for its royal pies — Michelin Bib Gourmand (Chicago 2024).
Old Irving Park's benchmark barbecue — Michelin Bib Gourmand and one of Eater Chicago's 38 essential restaurants.
The Carbajal family's Pilsen carnitas house since 1975, 'arguably the most famous taqueria in Chicago'; the original is a carry-out counter.
Little Village grocery-counter taquería widely ranked among Chicago's very best tacos.
Below-street River North tiki bar — #27 on the World's 50 Best Bars (2014).
Ukrainian Village dive since 1935 — Nelson Algren's haunt, famous neon sign and photo booth.
Old Town dive by Second City — walls of regulars' portraits, a Bourdain favourite.
Tony Hu's original Chinatown Sichuan house, through a side gate off Archer.
Greek taverna just off Logan Square Park — in the Michelin Guide.
Boka Group's West Loop Japanese canteen with multiple kitchens (exec. chef Gene Kato) — in the Michelin Guide.
Chef Sangtae Park's intimate West Loop omakase — in the Michelin Guide.
Chef Erick Williams's Hyde Park Southern restaurant within view of the University of Chicago — Michelin Bib Gourmand 2025; Eater Chicago 38.
Sichuan restaurant — Michelin Bib Gourmand 2024 and 2025.
Sleek Chinatown restaurant with a full bar — Michelin-listed; 'diners would do well to try the impressive specialty menu'.
Andersonville Belgian beer bar — Time Out Chicago's Best Beer Bar; a fixture of Chicago craft-beer guides.
Andersonville bakery-café honouring the neighbourhood's Swedish roots (chef Bobby Schaffer mills his own flour).
Bridgeport Italian institution since 1946 whose 1976 breaded steak sandwich Bourdain featured on Parts Unknown.
Wicker Park's modern Greek — no Greektown kitsch, refined regional cooking.

Beverly Kim and Johnny Clark's highly personal Korean-American restaurant in Avondale — one of the most creative rooms in town — CLOSED 23 Mar 2024 after 10 years (Michelin star 2014–21, James Beard 2019); the space is now the chefs' casual Parachute HiFi music bar.
West Loop diner whose cheeseburger Thrillist ranked among America's best — the most hyped burger in Chicago.
Taylor Street summer-only Italian-ice stand since 1954 — one of Chicago Magazine's 50 Iconic Eats.

places.ad: 1073 W Vernon Park Pl, Chicago, IL 60607
places.w: Little Italy tavern founded 1930 by Joseph and Teresa DiBuono — James Beard America's Classics Award (2008).
Ukrainian Village's Old-World Ukrainian kitchen (opened 2016) — the Infatuation's pick for a varenyky-and-vodka night.

places.ad: 2340 N California Ave, Unit B, Chicago, IL 60647
places.w: Logan Square ramen counter from Mike Satinover — Reddit's 'Ramen Lord' of r/ramen — on Bon Appétit's 20 best new restaurants of 2024 and the NYT's 25 best in Chicago.
Bridgeport's tavern-style institution since 1960 — greasy, generously topped thin pies cut in squares, counter service, cash only.
South Siders' pick for the city's best beef — one of the biggest sandwiches in town, thicker slices that stay tender (Infatuation 8.0).
Beverly's wood-panelled burger shop since 1942 — fresh-ground round on a feather-light bun, fries cooked in beef tallow.
Pilsen carnitas house opened by Pedro Duarte in 1981 — pork cooked in its own fat, sold by weight; weekend lines out the door.
Cicero corner grocery turned Italian deli-pizzeria, run by Neapolitan immigrant Joe Quercia since 1973 — hot-table Italian, pizza and some of the area's best gelato.
Senegalese family restaurant (2004, Bronzeville since 2015) — called one of the city's best African restaurants; South Side Weekly's 'Best Resurrection' after a fire.
Chicago-style aquarium-smoker barbecue, in Bronzeville since 2015 — a Choose Chicago South Side pick. Cash only.
Bronzeville soul-food dining room since 1993 — Roadfood rates it 'Excellent / Worth a Detour'.
Evanston barbecue institution of the late Hecky Powell — the North Shore's rib-tip and sauce benchmark (Axios rib-tip Food Fight).
The 1960 Wilmette original of the North Shore pancake family (in Ordinary People) — Zagat's 'best breakfast, bar none'.

places.ad: 1621 N Thatcher Ave, Elmwood Park, IL 60707
places.w: Opened 1930 — the oldest continuously operating barbecue restaurant in the Chicago area, on Thatcher Avenue since the 1940s.
The 1971 original of Lou Malnati's — where the family's buttercrust deep dish began, before it became Chicago's best-known deep-dish name.
Berwyn roots-music club and tavern (FitzGerald family since 1980, a music hall since the 1930s) — in 2025 the first Illinois music venue on the National Register.

places.ad: 8249 S Cottage Grove Ave, Chicago, IL 60619
places.w: Chatham's round-the-clock donut shop — its glazed made the Daily Meal's America's 25 best; often called the best donuts on the South Side.
The 1923 Little Village tavern (named for baseballs through its window) where Home Run Inn pizza began in 1947 — the brand that founded National Tavern-Style Pizza Day.
Archer Avenue's 24-hour donut-and-diner counter, on Time Out's list of old-school Chicago doughnut shops.
Evanston's European-style bakery since 1938 — ~700 customers a day for strudel, Danish and Fat Tuesday pączki.
Pullman smokehouse of Dominique Leach, 2023 'Master of 'Cue' on Food Network's BBQ Brawl — one of the city's best barbecue spots.
Little Village's unlikely al pastor champion — a Chinese-Thai takeout counter whose trompo makes some of the best al pastor in Chicago.
Austin's soul-food cafeteria (1997) of Mississippi-born MacArthur Alexander — a West Side institution whose regulars included Barack Obama.
University Village corner stand (since 1929) — the Infatuation calls its jus the best in Chicago; cash-only ice counter next door.
Pilsen's Green-Restaurant-certified bar and cultural space — solar panels, salvaged fittings, a bar made from a bowling lane.
Casual, affordable Pilsen BYOB from chef Alfonso Sotelo (ex-Bayless) — Michelin-listed regional Mexican cooking.
Milwaukee-area custard stand since 1950 — one of the city's 'big three' with Gilles and Leon's; the Greenfield store is the original HQ.
Pilsen birrieria with a half-dozen-item menu — Time Out: 'one visit to this one before you stop caring about the rest.'
One of Pilsen's first coffeehouse-galleries (1994), opened by Eleazar Delgado in an old barber shop at 18th & Bishop — a neighbourhood living room for artists.
Where Ike Sewell's 1943 pizzeria is credited with launching Chicago deep dish — the original still stands at Ohio & Wabash.
River North steakhouse (1987) named for the Cubs broadcaster, in a building once home to Capone enforcer Frank Nitti.
Rush Street power steakhouse since 1989 — consistently among the top-grossing independent restaurants in the US.
One of America's oldest continuously operating lunch-car diners (1926), hauled to Kenosha by six horses — on the National Register.
Milwaukee's neon-lit custard stand since the 1940s — said to have inspired Arnold's on Happy Days.

places.ad: 4629 N Port Washington Rd, Glendale, WI 53212
places.w: Glendale diner (1936) thought to have created the Wisconsin butter burger.
Puerto Rican-owned bakery-café on Paseo Boricua a block from Humboldt Park — some of the city's best Puerto Rican coffee and pastries.
The big Balmoral brewery and taproom (2017) of Half Acre, a staple of Chicago craft brewing since 2006.
Lakeview dive at Clark & Belmont since the 1950s — Irish whiskey selection, a dark lore, and a stop on Anthony Bourdain's The Layover.
Six-table Edgewater counter where masa is patted and griddled to order — called the best huaraches in Chicago. Cash only.
Paul Kahan's 2008 Fulton Market beer hall of pork, oysters and beer — the restaurant that helped turn the meatpacking district into a dining destination.
James Beard-winning chef Sarah Grueneberg's West Loop pasta house (2015), with sheets rolled and hung daily in view of the counter.
Beverly's neon-trimmed 1960 drive-in, revived in 2014 with its classic décor and menu intact — featured on Chicago's Best.
Yelitza Rivera's Logan Square corner (2016) with the widest jibarito menu in town — lines out the door, now with a sit-down room next door.
Ravenswood's Neapolitan pizzeria with a quiet side-street patio — No. 14 in 50 Top Pizza USA 2023 and on its world top-100.
Loop pub since 1935 under the Wabash 'L' — signed photos from Sinatra to Monroe and one of the Loop's few late-night kitchens.
Lincoln Park's retro-pastel bakery — the city's go-to for old-fashioned buttercream cupcakes and bars.
Wrigleyville's best-known Cubs bar — a 1930s hot-dog stand (Ernie's, then Ray's Bleachers) facing the bleacher entrance at Sheffield & Waveland.
Derrick Tung's Logan Square outpost of the Brooklyn pizzeria — his Detroit-style square won the 2018 U.S. Pizza Cup; a fixture of Time Out's essential-pizza list.
Family-run Loop pub since 1969 in a reputed Capone-era speakeasy — a less-crowded deep-dish alternative a block from Miller's Pub.
Mexican seafood house tucked into Thalia Hall from the Obelix / Taqueria Chingón team — whole fish from a wood-burning oven with tortillas and salsas.
Chef Thai Dang's 'unapologetically authentic' Vietnamese dining room in Pilsen — a James Beard-semifinalist kitchen and neighbourhood mainstay.

places.ad: 4248 S Cottage Grove Ave, Chicago, IL
places.w: Chef Kristen Harper's Creole-leaning Bronzeville soul-food counter — some of Chicago's best wings and fried chicken; Keith Lee's only 10/10 on his 2023 Chicago tour.
Chinatown's soup-dumpling specialist — xiaolongbao made fresh daily in full view of the dining room.

places.ad: 5200 S Archer Ave, Unit 8, Chicago, IL 60632
places.w: Family-run Archer Heights counter where scratch masa is the star — tlacoyos, picaditas, sopes and giant quesadillas (Infatuation 9.4).
Little Village taqueria that grew from Adan Lucido's home pop-up — al pastor carved to order off the spit with pineapple and salsa.
McKinley Park warehouse taproom from the Maria's/Kimski family — wraparound bar, brewhouse views, arcade, karaoke and comedy nights.
Devon Avenue's beloved cheap-eats institution — rich Indian/Pakistani plates at rock-bottom prices, open late.
Long-running Argyle Street Vietnamese dining room prized for consistency — shaking beef, tapioca dumplings, bún bò Huế.
Bridgeport Cantonese seafood house from the Wing Yip family — live-tank shellfish and wok-fried lobster over lap-cheong sticky rice.
Family bakery since 1930 (founded at 45th & Kedzie) — the Garfield Ridge institution of German/Polish/Scandinavian-rooted sweets; named Illinois' best bakery.
Family-run European bakery founded 1943, one of the Garfield Ridge Polish bakeries that survived — a Paczki Day pilgrimage.
Brighton Park taqueria spun out of Paco Francisco's La Internacional taco stand — about 3,000 tacos a day, voted among the city's best.

places.n: La Internacional (Back of the Yards taqueria)
places.w: The early-'80s supermercado whose back-of-store taco stand became a destination — the original Paco's Tacos operation.
One of the city's oldest taquerias (founded 1972 by Don Jesús from Arandas, Jalisco), cash-only and open till 3–4am on weekends.
Bucktown's 'travelers' tavern' since 1992 — maps on the walls, a beer list you can't fit another bottle on.
